verses.1:1: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have observed closely and our hands have touched, concerning the word of life;
verses.1:2: and the life was revealed, and we have seen, and we testify, and we proclaim to you eternal life, which was with the Father and appeared to us;
verses.1:3: what we have seen and heard, we proclaim to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us, and that our fellowship may be with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: And we are writing these things to you so that you may rejoice, and that your joy may be full.
verses.1:5: And this is the proclamation that we have heard from Him and proclaim to you: that God is light, and there is not any darkness in Him.
verses.1:6: If we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness, we are lying and do not do the truth.
verses.1:7: But if we walk in the light, just as He Himself also is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ, His Son, cleanses us from all sin.
verses.1:8: If we say that we do not have sin, we are deceiving ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
verses.1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous, so that He will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all iniquity.
verses.1:10: If we say that we have not sinned, we are making Him a liar, and His word is not in us.
verses.2:1: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. Yet even if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
verses.2:2: And He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, yet not for ours only, but also for those of the entire world.
verses.2:3: And by this we know that we have come to know Him, if we observe His commandments.
verses.2:4: The one who says that he knows Him and does not keep His commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
verses.2:5: But whoever keeps His word, truly in him the love of God is perfected; and by this we know that we are in Him.
verses.2:6: The one who says that he remains in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.
verses.2:7: Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment that you have had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you have heard.
verses.2:8: Again, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true both in Him and in you, because the darkness has passed away and the true light is already shining.
verses.2:9: The one who says that he is in the light and hates his brother is in darkness even until now.
verses.2:10: The one who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no stumbling block in him.
verses.2:11: But the one who hates his brother is in darkness, and walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
verses.2:12: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for the sake of His name.
verses.2:13: I am writing to you, fathers, because you have come to know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, youths, because you have overcome the evil one.
verses.2:14: I am writing to you, young children, because you have come to know the Father. I am writing to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
verses.2:15: Do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
verses.2:16: For everything that is in the world is the craving of the flesh, and the craving of the eyes, and the pride of life, which is not from the Father, but is from the world.
verses.2:17: And the world is passing away, and its craving; yet the one who does the will of God remains forever.
verses.2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and just as you heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen; from this we know that it is the last hour.
verses.2:19: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us; rather, so that they might be clearly revealed, that they are not all of us.
verses.2:20: But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things.
verses.2:21: I have not written to you as to those ignorant of the truth, but as to those who know it, and that no lie is from the truth.
verses.2:22: Who is the liar except the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son.
verses.2:23: Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; the one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
verses.2:24: As for you, let what you heard from the beginning continue to remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning continues to remain in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father.
verses.2:25: And this is the promise that He Himself promised us: eternal life.
verses.2:26: I have written these things to you concerning those who would deceive you.
verses.2:27: And as for you, let the anointing that you received from Him remain in you. And you have no need for anyone to teach you; rather, as His anointing teaches you concerning all things, it is both true and not a lie. And just as it has taught you, remain in Him.
verses.2:28: And now, little children, remain in Him, so that when He appears we may have confidence and not be put to shame by Him at His coming.
verses.2:29: If you know that He is righteous, know also that everyone who does righteousness has been born of Him.
verses.3:1: See what sort of love the Father has given us, that we may be called and be children of God. Because of this, the world does not know us, for it does not know Him.
verses.3:2: Beloved, we are now children of God, and it has not yet appeared what we will be. We know that once He appears, we will be like Him, since we will see Him as He is.
verses.3:3: And everyone who has this hope in Him sanctifies himself, just as He also is holy.
verses.3:4: Everyone who commits sin also commits iniquity, and sin is iniquity.
verses.3:5: And you know that He appeared in order to take away our sins, and there is no sin in Him.
verses.3:6: Everyone who remains in Him does not sin; and everyone who sins has not seen Him, nor come to know Him.
verses.3:7: Little children, let no one deceive you. The one who does righteousness is righteous, just as He also is righteous.
verses.3:8: The one who commits sin is of the devil, because the devil sins from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God appeared: to undo the works of the devil.
verses.3:9: Everyone who has been born of God does not commit sin, because His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
verses.3:10: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are clearly revealed: everyone who is not righteous is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
verses.3:11: For this is the proclamation that you have heard from the beginning: that you should love one another.
verses.3:12: Not like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And for what reason did he kill him? Because his works were evil, while his brother's were righteous.
verses.3:13: Do not be amazed, brothers, if the world hates you.
verses.3:14: We know that we have been transferred from death to life, because we love the brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
verses.3:15: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in himself.
verses.3:16: By this we have come to know the love of God, that He laid down His life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.
verses.3:17: Whoever has the goods of this world and sees his brother in need, and shuts his compassion against him, how does the love of God remain in him?
verses.3:18: My little children, let us not love in word or in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
verses.3:19: By this we know that we are of the truth, and in His sight we will persuade our hearts.
verses.3:20: For if our heart reproaches us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.
verses.3:21: Beloved, if our heart does not reproach us, we have confidence toward God.
verses.3:22: And whatever we ask, we will receive from Him, because we keep His commandments and do the things that are pleasing before Him.
verses.3:23: And this is His commandment: that we should believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as He gave us a commandment.
verses.3:24: And the one who keeps His commandments remains in Him, and He Himself in him; and by this we know that He remains in us, from the Spirit whom He has given to us.
verses.4:1: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see if they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
verses.4:2: By this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God;
verses.4:3: and every spirit that dissolves Jesus is not from God, and this is the antichrist, concerning whom you have heard that he is coming, and now he is already in the world.
verses.4:4: You are from God, little children, and you have conquered him, because He who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.
verses.4:5: They are of the world; therefore they speak of the world, and the world listens to them.
verses.4:6: We are from God. The one who knows God listens to us; the one who is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
verses.4:7: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. And everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
verses.4:8: The one who does not love does not know God, because God is love.
verses.4:9: In this the love of God appeared in us: that God sent His only-begotten Son into the world, so that we may live through Him.
verses.4:10: In this is love: not as though we loved God, but that He Himself first loved us and sent His Son as a propitiation for our sins.
verses.4:11: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
verses.4:12: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us.
verses.4:13: By this we know that we remain in Him and He in us, because He has given us of His Spirit.
verses.4:14: And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent His Son as Savior of the world.
verses.4:15: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.
verses.4:16: And we have come to know and have believed the love that God has in us. God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God in him.
verses.4:17: In this the love of God has been perfected with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because just as He is, we also are in this world.
verses.4:18: There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear, because fear has punishment; and the one who fears is not perfected in love.
verses.4:19: Let us therefore love God, because God first loved us.
verses.4:20: If anyone says, "I love God," and hates his brother, he is a liar. For the one who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
verses.4:21: And we have this commandment from God: that the one who loves God should also love his brother.
verses.5:1: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. And everyone who loves Him who brought forth also loves the one who has been born of Him.
verses.5:2: By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and do His commandments.
verses.5:3: For this is the love of God: that we observe His commandments, and His commandments are not heavy.
verses.5:4: For everything that has been born of God conquers the world; and this is the victory that conquers the world: our faith.
verses.5:5: Who is the one who conquers the world, except the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
verses.5:6: This is He who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ: not in water only, but in water and blood. And it is the Spirit who testifies that Christ is the truth.
verses.5:7: For there are three who give testimony in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one.
verses.5:8: And there are three who give testimony on earth: the spirit, and the water, and the blood; and these three are one.
verses.5:9: If we accept the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, which is greater: that He has testified concerning His Son.
verses.5:10: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God in himself. The one who does not believe the Son makes Him a liar, because he does not believe in the testimony that God has testified concerning His Son.
verses.5:11: And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.
verses.5:12: The one who has the Son has life; the one who does not have the Son does not have life.
verses.5:13: I write these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
verses.5:14: And this is the confidence that we have toward Him: that whatever we ask according to His will, He hears us.
verses.5:15: And we know that He hears us, whatever we ask; we know that we have the petitions that we request from Him.
verses.5:16: Let the one who knows that his brother is committing a sin not leading to death ask, and life will be given to him, to the one sinning not leading to death. There is a sin leading to death; I do not say that anyone should pray for that.
verses.5:17: All iniquity is sin, and there is a sin leading to death.
verses.5:18: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the generation of God preserves him, and the evil one does not touch him.
verses.5:19: We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the evil one.
verses.5:20: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true God and may be in His true Son. This is the true God and eternal life.
verses.5:21: Little children, guard yourselves from idols. Amen.

notes.1:3: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive sit ('may be'), coordinating this clause with habeatis under ut, whereas the Greek has no verb here and is usually read as indicative ('is').
notes.1:4: The Vulgate includes the clause ut gaudeatis ('so that you may rejoice'), which the Greek text lacks, and reads gaudium vestrum ('your joy') with part of the Greek tradition, whereas other Greek manuscripts read 'our joy.'
notes.1:7: The Vulgate reads Jesu Christi ('Jesus Christ'), whereas many critical Greek editions omit 'Christ.'
notes.2:8: The Vulgate uses the perfect tense transierunt ('has passed away'), contrasting with the Greek present paragetai ('is passing away') and the Vulgate's own present transit in 2:17.
notes.2:14: The Clementine Vulgate maintains the present tense Scribo ('I am writing') across 2:12-14 and omits the second address to 'fathers' found in the Greek text.
notes.2:20: The Vulgate reads nostis omnia ('you know all things'), reflecting the textual variant panta rather than pantes ('you all know').
notes.2:27: The Vulgate renders the ambiguous Greek verb menete unambiguously as an imperative, manete ('remain').
notes.3:1: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive simus ('and should be'), linking it to ut nominemur, whereas the Greek uses the indicative esmen ('and we are').
notes.3:3: The Vulgate reads sanctificat ... sanctus ('sanctifies ... holy'), where the Greek uses hagnizei ... hagnos ('purifies ... pure').
notes.3:4: The Vulgate renders Greek anomia ('lawlessness') as iniquitas ('iniquity'), matching iniquitate in 1:9.
notes.3:10: The Vulgate reads qui non est justus ('who is not righteous'), whereas the Greek reads 'who does not practice righteousness'; similarly, 3:11 uses second-person plural diligatis ('that you should love') rather than Greek first-person plural ('that we should love').
notes.3:16: The Vulgate explicitly reads caritatem Dei ('the love of God'), adding Dei where Greek manuscripts have simply 'love.'
notes.4:2: The Vulgate reads the passive 'cognoscitur' ('is known'), whereas the Greek text has the second-person plural 'ginoskete' ('you know').
notes.4:3: The Vulgate reads 'qui solvit Jesum' ('that dissolves Jesus,' reflecting the early reading 'lyei') rather than 'does not confess Jesus,' and renders the next clause directly as 'this is the antichrist' rather than 'the [spirit] of the antichrist.'
notes.4:4: The Vulgate uses the singular 'eum' ('him,' referring back to the antichrist of v. 3), whereas the Greek text has the plural 'autous' ('them,' referring to the false prophets).
notes.4:19: The Vulgate uses the hortatory subjunctive 'diligamus' ('let us love') with explicit 'Deum' ('God') and 'Deus' ('God'), whereas the Greek agapomen is usually read as indicative ('we love'), and most Greek manuscripts lack both explicit nouns.
notes.5:6: The Vulgate reads 'quoniam Christus est veritas' ('that Christ is the truth'), whereas the Greek manuscripts read 'that the Spirit is the truth.'
notes.5:7: Verses 7-8 contain the Johannine Comma ('in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one. And there are three who give testimony on earth'), a hallmark reading of the Clementine Vulgate absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.5:10: The Vulgate reads 'non credit Filio' ('does not believe the Son') and adds 'Dei' ('of God') after the first 'testimony,' whereas the Greek text reads 'does not believe God' and omits 'of God.'
notes.5:17: The Clementine Vulgate omits 'non' ('not'), reading 'et est peccatum ad mortem' ('and there is a sin leading to death'), whereas the Greek text reads 'and there is sin not leading to death.'
notes.5:18: The Vulgate renders the Greek participle 'the One born of God' abstractly as 'generatio Dei' ('the generation of God,' i.e., being born of God) preserving the believer.
notes.5:20: The Vulgate explicitly supplies 'Deum' ('the true God') and reads the subjunctive 'simus in vero Filio ejus' ('may be in His true Son'), without the closing name 'Jesus Christ' found in Greek manuscripts.
